verdicts.flaw_description: Rainfall in every plot's season was 'the highest on record, roughly double the year before' and every plot was 'watered by rain alone', so the doubled water supply is a live alternative cause that fits all four cases (8-13 cm gains); the comparison is against the previous, drier summer.

Two of the four cases have measurement dates that precede the intervention: case One was 'issued 4 November' but measured 'by 27 September', and case Three was 'issued 5 June' but measured 'by 28 April'. The outcome was recorded before the kit was in use.

Order volume 'hit a record low, half the earlier period' and 'every run carried whatever drop count the depot set', so the runs were exposed to the halved workload; fewer drops per run explains the 5-9 minute reduction independently of the routing change.

The claim is about absence, but every case measures lateness ('lateness ran 6 / 4 / 7 / 5 percent below the same cohort a term earlier'). Punctuality is not the quantity the claim is about; a cohort can be less late and no less absent.
